thread.title: Stocks Swing Lower As Disney Rises, Hertz Spikes| Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Swing Lower As Disney Rises, Hertz Spikes| Investor's Business Daily
text:
Tech stocks fell hardest despite a few bright spots Friday, as earnings news and a wave of overseas selling chewed into opening trade.
X Chip stocks were mixed, with Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) down hard on earnings and Cree ( CREE ) bolting higher on an analyst upgrade. FANG stocks dropped into the red early, with Netflix ( NFLX ) leading the declines. Apple ( AAPL ) fell on questions regarding iPhone XR sales, while Apple supplier Finisar ( FNSR ) surged on acquisition news.
On the earnings front, Yelp ( YELP ), Sierra Wireless ( SWIR ) and Activision Blizzard ( ATVI ) were among the morning's many steep early losses. Hertz Global ( HTZ ) spiked 16%. Revlon ( REV ) rocketed 22% higher. Among IBD 50 stocks , Globus Medical ( GMED ), Trade Desk ( TTD ) and China's Momo ( MOMO ) fell on earnings.
The Nasdaq Composite skidded 0.9% lower, with Activision and Skyworks taking two of the index's hardest early hits.
The S&P 500 retreated 0.5%, while Caterpillar ( CAT ), Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) and Apple dragged the Dow Jones industrial average 0.3% lower. Walt Disney ( DIS ) led the Dow after a strong fiscal fourth-quarter report .

Please contact customer service CLOSE Premarket Trading: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Face Resistance The market returned to a confirmed uptrend this week with the Nasdaq posting a post-election follow-through day on Wednesday. The Nasdaq heads into Friday's open up 2.4% in a second strong weekly advance off an Oct. 29 low. The Dow is up 3.6% and the S&P 500 has a 3.1% gain.
Technical resistance and support could play a part in Friday's market action. The Dow has decisively retaken support at both its 50- and 200-day moving averages. The S&P 500 is just set to test resistance at its 50-day line. The Nasdaq is attempting to hold support at its 200-day level, and remains 1% below its 50-day line.
Disney Streams Higher, Finisar Spikes On Takeover Fiber optic telecom play Finisar spiked 16% after laser products maker II-VI ( IIVI ) agreed to buy the company for $3.2 billion. The companies — both suppliers of 3D sensing components to Apple — expect the cash/stock deal to close in mid-2019. Finisar had climbed 13% through Thursday on speculation regarding a deal. II-VI shares dropped nearly 17% in premarket trade.
Disney jumped 2.7%, retaking the 118 level in premarket trade. That sent shares back above a 118 buy point — an entry the stock has been struggling to put behind it since September. Shares rose following a strong fiscal fourth quarter showing, plus new details on the launch of the media giant's pending Disney Plus streaming content platform .
LED lighting products maker Cree opened 3% higher, after Goldman Sachs shifted its rating to buy, from neutral. The note also placed a price target at 58, 44% above the stock's closing price on Thursday. The gain left shares testing Cree's 10-week moving average, as the stock attempts to climb the right side of a possible three-month base pattern .
On the downside, IBD 50 stock Trade Desk dropped 3% lower after reporting an above-forecast 86% gain in earnings and a 50% revenue increase in its third quarter. The loss signaled a continued resistance at the stock's 10-week moving average, below which it has traded for the past five weeks.
Japan, China Markets Dive; Europe Trims Losses A dive in October auto sales helped send China's markets sharply lower Friday. Losses were exacerbated by Thursday's loss on U.S. markets of Ctrip.com International ( CTRP ), which tanked 19% after the company's chief financial officer warned of "macro slowdown uncertainties" in the company's conference call.
The Hong Kong Hang Seng index dropped 2.4%, and the Shanghai Composite slipped 1.4% lower. Shanghai ended the week down 2.9%. The Hang Seng fell 3.3% as it pulled back from another test of resistance at its 50-day line.
Japan also turned lower, as the dollar climbed following Thursday's U.S. Fed decision, and after a release of minutes showed Bank of Japan policymakers concerned over U.S. economic growth and rising interest rates. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 slumped 1.1%, ending effectively flat for the week.
The selling initially carried over into Europe, but stocks pared early losses in afternoon trade. The CAC-40 in Paris was down 0.6%. The DAX in Frankfurt and London's FTSE 100 were off 0.1% and 0.6%, respectively.
Producer Prices Jump, Oil Prices Undercut $60 Oil prices appear set to factor into Friday's trade, as West Texas Intermediate dropped 1.8% — undercutting the $60 per barrel mark for the first time since March. Nine straight down days have left oil prices 22% below an early October high, and in their longest sustained downtrend since July 2014.
Rising U.S. supplies, U.S. waivers for countries buying oil from Iran, releases from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve and speculation ahead of the weekend meeting of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries all factor into the declines.
Growth in prices paid to producers accelerated in October, the Labor Department reported. October producers prices gained 0.6%, triple September's 0.2% gain, as well as analyst views for a 0.2% growth. Year-over-year, growth increased to 2.9%, up from 2.6% in September.
Core prices — minus energy and food — gained 0.5%, up from a 0.2% gain in September and vs. forecasts for another 0.2% rise.
Preliminary consumer sentiment for November, and wholesale inventory numbers are expected after the start of trade. Baker Hughes ( BHGE ) releases its weekly rig count census at 1 p.m. ET.
